subdomain: 4.3 Conduct A/B testing and iterative improvements

en.question: A tool-planning change fixes several difficult tasks in a capability suite. The product already supports a large set of simpler workflows, and the team wants an iterative release process rather than optimizing only for the new cases. Which actions support that goal? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Run the established regression suite alongside the new capability cases.
options.note: Capability improvements do not show that previously supported workflows still work. The regression suite checks that existing behavior survives the planning change.

options.text: Promote reproducibly solved capability cases into ongoing regression coverage.
options.note: Once a difficult behavior is reliably supported, keeping it in regression coverage protects the improvement during later iterations. This turns a demonstrated capability into a maintained contract.

options.text: Remove older successful cases so the suite concentrates on remaining failures.
options.note: Removing supported cases loses the ability to detect regressions in them. A capability-focused backlog and a regression suite answer different questions and should coexist.

options.text: Use the new capability pass rate as the release score for all workflows.
options.note: A suite selected for difficult new tasks is not evidence about every existing workflow. Its score cannot substitute for checking the behavior the product already promises.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
